obligation: County contract incident notice
trigger: Suspected or confirmed security incident affecting county systems, data, or buildings (including SYS-01 and the county gateways)
deadline: Within 24 hours of discovery
notify: County IT security officer and county facilities director
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual

obligation: City contract incident notice
trigger: Suspected or confirmed security incident affecting city systems, data, or buildings (including company accounts on SYS-10 and the city gateways)
deadline: Within 24 hours of discovery
notify: City IT manager and city facilities manager
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual

obligation: Notice to the prime for GSA systems, data, or credentials
citation: CT-F subcontract; GSA BTTRG v3.0 section 1.6.1; C-GOVERNMENT-R01
trigger: Potential incident involving GSA building systems, GSA data (including CUI drawings and FCI), or a PIV card or GSA credential of company staff
deadline: Immediately on discovery, so the prime can report to GSA IT immediately
notify: Prime contractor security officer and project manager
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if GSA systems, data, CUI, or credentials may be involved

obligation: County's own report to the state (customer duty)
trigger: County determines a ransomware incident or a severity level 3, 4, or 5 cybersecurity incident
deadline: County reports as soon as possible, no later than 48 hours after discovery (12 hours for ransomware); the company's notice must arrive well before that
notify: Cybersecurity Operations Center, FDLE Cybercrime Office, and the sheriff (by the county); company supplies the facts in 282.3185(5)(a): summary, last backup date and location, data types, estimated fiscal impact
applies_at_this_tier: Customer duty - company supports with facts and timeline

obligation: City's own report to the state (customer duty)
trigger: City determines a ransomware incident or a severity level 3, 4, or 5 cybersecurity incident
deadline: City reports no later than 48 hours after discovery (12 hours for ransomware)
notify: Cybersecurity Operations Center, FDLE Cybercrime Office, and the sheriff (by the city); company supplies facts
applies_at_this_tier: Customer duty - company supports

obligation: County or city after-action report (customer duty)
trigger: Remediation of a cybersecurity or ransomware incident
deadline: Customer submits within 1 week after remediation
notify: Florida Digital Service (by the customer); company supplies input
applies_at_this_tier: Customer duty - company supports

obligation: Third-party agent breach notice to the customer
trigger: Breach of security of a system the company maintains that holds personal information for a customer (SYS-01: cardholder names with badge credential numbers, access history, or face templates; which fields count is for counsel to confirm)
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable, no later than 10 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe it occurred (the 24-hour contract notice comes first)
notify: The county, with all information it needs for its own notices
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - company is a third-party agent; counsel confirms whether the county is a governmental entity under 501.171(1)(f)

obligation: Florida breach notice to individuals (company data)
trigger: Breach of the company's own personal information (employee SSNs, bank details, background check results)
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe it occurred (a 15-day extension is possible only with written good cause to the Department within 30 days)
notify: Affected Florida residents by mail or email
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - company is a covered entity for its own data

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs
applies_at_this_tier: Company data: no (fewer than 20 current and former employees). SYS-01 data (about 1,050 cardholders): the county decides as the notifying entity; company supplies information

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at one time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay
notify: Nationwide consumer reporting agencies
applies_at_this_tier: Possible for SYS-01 data (about 1,050 cardholders); the county decides; not for company data

obligation: State data breach notification (other states)
trigger: Affected cardholders or employees who live outside Florida
deadline: Varies by state
notify: Residents and regulators under each state's law
applies_at_this_tier: Check residency of affected people; apply each state's law where affected individuals reside

obligation: Covered telecommunications or video surveillance equipment found
citation: FAR 52.204-25(d) (Section 889), as flowed down; FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Covered equipment identified as a substantial or essential component of anything supplied under CT-F
deadline: Within one business day of identification; further information within 10 business days. Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
notify: Prime contractor, which reports to the GSA contracting officer
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - CT-F clause

obligation: Kaspersky covered article found
citation: FAR 52.204-23(c), as flowed down; FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Kaspersky covered article identified in anything provided under CT-F
deadline: Within 3 business days of identification; further information within 10 business days. Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
notify: Prime contractor, which reports to the GSA contracting officer
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - CT-F clause

obligation: FASCSA order article found
citation: FAR 52.204-30(c)(3)-(4), as flowed down; FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Covered article or source subject to a FASCSA order provided or used under CT-F
deadline: Within 3 business days of identification; further information within 10 business days. Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
notify: Prime contractor, which reports to the GSA contracting officer
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - CT-F clause

obligation: Ransom payment restrictions and OFAC sanctions check
citation: Fla. Stat. 282.3186; OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Ransom demand
deadline: Counties and municipalities may not pay or otherwise comply with a ransom demand; the company will not pay on their behalf. Any company payment for its own systems needs an OFAC sanctions check first
notify: OFAC (license if a sanctioned party); FBI or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Yes

obligation: Voluntary report to law enforcement and CISA
trigger: Intrusion into building control or access control systems
deadline: As soon as practical, coordinated with the customer (full and timely reporting is an OFAC mitigating factor)
notify: FBI field office or IC3; CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Recommended

obligation: Cyber insurance claim notice
trigger: Suspected security incident
deadline: Prompt notice through the 24x7 breach hotline, before engaging any outside firm
notify: Carrier breach hotline (panel counsel and forensics assigned)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual

obligation: MSP incident notice to the company
citation: MSP contract (no incident notice term today; 24-hour term in the planned security addendum, POAM-005)
trigger: Incident affecting the MSP, its RMM platform, or company laptops
deadline: None today; 24 hours once the addendum is signed
notify: Office and Compliance Manager
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - gap until the addendum is signed

obligation: Access control vendor incident notice to the company
trigger: Security incident affecting the company tenant or county data
deadline: Within 72 hours of the vendor confirming the incident (24 hours requested at renewal)
notify: Office and Compliance Manager and Security Systems Technician
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - inbound

obligation: FTI unauthorized disclosure / data breach
trigger: Unauthorized disclosure of federal tax information
deadline: Immediately, no later than 24 hours after discovery
notify: TIGTA and IRS Office of Safeguards
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company handles no FTI (C-GOVERNMENT-R02 not in scope)

obligation: CJIS incident reporting (IR-6)
trigger: Incident involving criminal justice information
deadline: Report to the incident response capability immediately, and no more than 1 hour after discovery
notify: Agency incident handlers and CJIS contacts
applies_at_this_tier: No - no criminal justice buildings or CJI in scope (C-GOVERNMENT-R03)

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reports (proposed)
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours (incident); 24 hours after a ransom payment
notify: CISA
applies_at_this_tier: No - final rule not published as of 2026-09-25; the company is far below its SBA size standard and the proposed government facilities criteria cover government entities, not contractors; recheck when final
